name: INS_CockpitAlloc
returns: int: new cockpit handle (>=1), 0 if the cockpit could not be allocated
summary: Creates a new cockpit (view controller with its own cockpit scene, camera and lights) and returns its handle.
semantics: Allocates a Cockpit (AP 0x810 bytes, FL 0x8c0) and runs Cockpit::Ctor, then Cockpit::CreateScene: a new 3D scene named 'Cockpit Scene' (cockpit scene scale), a scene camera (camFlags |= 0x24, at the origin, identity rotation, attached to that scene) and 16 directional light nodes (grey 0x80,0x80,0x80, at z=131.072 m). The cockpit is registered under the next free automatic id of the registry's hash map (ids 1..max, the counter only grows and wraps; a freed id is not reused until the wrap) and the id is returned. Defaults set by the ctor: viewMode 0, connectMode 0, cockpitNumber 0, monitorNumber -1, radarMode 1, radarRange 10000000 (20 km), flags 0, cinematicLoopTime 15000 ms, enable2DDraw 1, noDecay 0, zoom 1.0, currentMissile -1, sectorFov = the registry's base FOV (INS_SetFocus), tracking cleared, all reference objects, sector and sector/galaxy/dust cameras NULL. The script owns the cockpit: it lives until INS_CockpitFree; it is saved with the game (cockpit section of the savegame, the handle is kept) so a handle stays valid across save/load. Nothing is displayed until the script gives it cameras (INS_CockpitSetSectorCamera etc.), a reference object and a view mode; Cockpit::Update drives it every frame. If the allocation fails the answer is 0 (no cockpit).
fl: same (FL cockpit object is larger, 0x8c0 bytes: FL adds the LFL pointer drift state)

name: INS_CockpitFree
summary: Destroys a cockpit created by INS_CockpitAlloc.
semantics: All INS arguments are read as raw cell dwords (types are not checked); a cockpit handle is looked up with Cockpit::FindByHandle in the registry's hash map. If the handle is known: removes it from the registry hash map, runs Cockpit::Dtor (releases the cockpit scene, its camera, lights, HUD parts, tooltip etc.) and frees the memory. Unknown/0 handle: nothing. Always answers 0. Cameras set with INS_CockpitSet*Camera are not owned by the cockpit (they belong to the script's own scenes) and stay. After the call the handle is dead: every other INS_Cockpit* native treats it as unknown (INS_CockpitSetTracking then never answers, see that native).

name: INS_CockpitGetCamera
returns: int: node handle of the cockpit scene's own camera, 0 for an unknown cockpit
summary: Returns the handle of the camera of the cockpit's own (interior) scene.
semantics: All INS arguments are read as raw cell dwords (types are not checked); a cockpit handle is looked up with Cockpit::FindByHandle in the registry's hash map. Answers sceneCamera->node.handle (the camera created by INS_CockpitAlloc inside the cockpit scene; it renders the cockpit interior/HUD bodies). Unknown cockpit -> 0. The handle can be used with B3D_Camera* natives; the camera is owned by the cockpit.

name: INS_CockpitEnableCamera
summary: Attaches (enable) or detaches (disable) the cockpit scene's camera to/from the cockpit scene.
semantics: All INS arguments are read as raw cell dwords (types are not checked); a cockpit handle is looked up with Cockpit::FindByHandle in the registry's hash map. arg2 through CellIsTrue. true: if the cockpit, its scene camera and scene exist and the camera is not in the cockpit scene, Scene::AttachCamera(camera, cockpitScene) - the cockpit scene is rendered again. false: if the camera is currently in the cockpit scene, Scene::DetachCamera - the cockpit interior/HUD scene is no longer rendered. Repeated calls are no-ops. Answers 0 in all cases.

name: INS_CockpitGetScene

summary: Returns the handle of the cockpit's own 3D scene ('Cockpit Scene').
semantics: All INS arguments are read as raw cell dwords (types are not checked); a cockpit handle is looked up with Cockpit::FindByHandle in the registry's hash map. Answers cockpitScene->handle. name: INS_CockpitSetSectorCamera
summary: Sets the camera the cockpit drives for the sector (space) view.
semantics: All INS arguments are read as raw cell dwords (types are not checked); a cockpit handle is looked up with Cockpit::FindByHandle in the registry's hash map. camera = Scene::FindEnabledNodeById(arg2): the node with that handle if it has the camera flag, else NULL (so 0 or a non-camera handle clears it). Stores it in cockpit->sectorCamera and, if not NULL, sets the camera's focus (FOV) to the cockpit's sectorFov. Cockpit::Update then places and orients this camera from the view state every frame and keeps its FOV (zoom). The cockpit does not own the camera; scripts must clear it (0) before freeing the camera. Unknown cockpit: nothing. Answers 0. INS_CockpitProjectPosition needs this camera.

name: INS_CockpitSetGalaxyCamera
summary: Sets the camera the cockpit drives for the galaxy background (sky) scene.
semantics: All INS arguments are read as raw cell dwords (types are not checked); a cockpit handle is looked up with Cockpit::FindByHandle in the registry's hash map. Same as INS_CockpitSetSectorCamera but for cockpit->galaxyCamera (the camera of the background/galaxy scene that is rotated with the view): camera node by handle (camera flag required, else NULL), stored, and its focus set to sectorFov when not NULL. Not owned by the cockpit. Unknown cockpit: nothing. Answers 0.

name: INS_CockpitSetDustCamera

semantics: All INS arguments are read as raw cell dwords (types are not checked); a cockpit handle is looked up with Cockpit::FindByHandle in the registry's hash map. The flag is not removed when the camera is later replaced. Not owned by the cockpit. Used together with INS_InitDustScene / INS_UpdateDustScene. Unknown cockpit: nothing. Answers 0.

Only if both cockpit and sector are found: cockpit->sector = sector and Cockpit::ApplySectorAmbientColor - if the cockpit scene exists and the object really is a sector (class Space), the cockpit scene's ambient colour is set to the sector background's colour (background type table). summary: Sets the cockpit's reference object (the object the view is attached to / looks at).
semantics: All INS arguments are read as raw cell dwords (types are not checked); a cockpit handle is looked up with Cockpit::FindByHandle in the registry's hash map. object = 0 if arg2 == 0, else Object::FindByIdInWorld(arg2) (NULL if not found - an unknown id clears the field). If the cockpit is known: cockpit->refObject = object. refObject is the object an external/target view is built around and the object of connect modes (e.g. Flyby tests its speed); compare INS_CockpitSetCockpitRefObject (the ship whose cockpit/HUD it is). This object is the 'ship' of the cockpit: view origin and view points (INS_CockpitSetCockpitNumber), cockpit body/sway, scanner, gravidar and hostile search, zoom (only in view mode 1), distance readouts all need it; with NULL most of the HUD is not drawn. Answers 0.

name: INS_CockpitMoveCockpit
summary: Hides (value 1) or shows (any other value) all cockpit bodies at once: cockpit body, radar body and display body.
semantics: All INS arguments are read as raw cell dwords (types are not checked); a cockpit handle is looked up with Cockpit::FindByHandle in the registry's hash map. Cockpit::SetMoveCockpit(&cockpit->model, arg2): b = (arg2 != 1); model.cockpitBodyEnabled = radarBodyEnabled = displayBodyEnabled = b. So 1 turns the three body kinds off, 0 (or 2, -1, ...) turns all three on - note the inverted meaning against the name. The same flags are set one by one by INS_CockpitEnableCockpitBody / EnableRadarBody / EnableDisplayBody. Unknown cockpit: nothing. Answers 0.

name: INS_CockpitSetCockpitNumber
summary: Selects which view point (cockpit seat / turret) of the cockpit ship the view uses.
semantics: All INS arguments are read as raw cell dwords (types are not checked); a cockpit handle is looked up with Cockpit::FindByHandle in the registry's hash map. cockpit->cockpitNumber = arg2, a negative value is stored as 0. The number indexes the view points of the ship type of cockpitRefObject (0 = main cockpit, higher = turret/gun view points; count from the ship type's view point count); out-of-range numbers make the view fall back to the ship's root position (Cockpit::GetViewOrigin) and no gun group. Unknown cockpit: nothing. Answers 0.

summary: Returns the cockpit's selected view point number.
semantics: All INS arguments are read as raw cell dwords (types are not checked); a cockpit handle is looked up with Cockpit::FindByHandle in the registry's hash map. Answers cockpit->cockpitNumber (default 0); unknown cockpit -> 0.

summary: Sets the monitor index of the cockpit (0 = main screen).
semantics: All INS arguments are read as raw cell dwords (types are not checked); a cockpit handle is looked up with Cockpit::FindByHandle in the registry's hash map. cockpit->monitorNumber = arg2 (raw, no clamp; default -1). Monitor 0 is the main view: e.g. target cycling (INS_CockpitTargetOverlayTrackPrevNext) only works for the cockpit with monitor number 0. Unknown cockpit: nothing. Answers 0.

name: INS_CockpitDisplayMessage
summary: Shows a text in the cockpit's text panel (a non-string clears it).
semantics: All INS arguments are read as raw cell dwords (types are not checked); a cockpit handle is looked up with Cockpit::FindByHandle in the registry's hash map. text = the string of arg2 if it is a string cell (type 2 or 0xb), else NULL. Hud::ShowTextPanel61(&cockpit->textPanel, text): shows the text (NULL hides the panel). The display duration field is NOT touched (whatever INS_CockpitDisplayMessageWithDuration set last stays). Unknown cockpit: nothing. Answers 0.

summary: Shows a text in the cockpit's text panel for a given time.
semantics: All INS arguments are read as raw cell dwords (types are not checked); a cockpit handle is looked up with Cockpit::FindByHandle in the registry's hash map. If arg2 is a string cell: Hud::ShowTextPanel61(textPanel, text) and then textPanelDuration (timeout) = arg3 (ms, raw). Not a string: the panel is cleared (ShowTextPanel61 with NULL) and the duration set to 0. Unknown cockpit: nothing. Answers 0.

name: INS_CockpitSetZooming
summary: Requests the cockpit zoom (non-zero) or its release (0); the zoom itself runs in the cockpit update.
semantics: All INS arguments are read as raw cell dwords (types are not checked); a cockpit handle is looked up with Cockpit::FindByHandle in the registry's hash map. Sets (arg2 != 0) or clears (arg2 == 0) bit 0 of cockpit->zoomFlags. Cockpit update (only while cockpitRefObject is set and viewMode == 1, the cockpit view): with bit 0 set it starts a zoom to twice the current zoom over 1000 ms (sound 0x3d3), so repeated requests zoom further (2x, 4x, ...); bit 0 is cleared again every frame by the update, so the script sets it once per zoom step. Without the request and zoom != 1 the zoom returns to 1x (ramp between 2 and 3 s, sound 0x3d3). The FOV of the scene and sector cameras is the base FOV divided by the zoom. Unknown cockpit: nothing. Answers 0.

name: INS_SetTimeWarpFactor
summary: Stores a time-warp factor in the cockpit registry (does not change the game speed by itself).
semantics: No cockpit handle. CockpitRegistry->timeWarpFactor = arg1 (raw 16.16 value). In the code read, this registry field is only written here, zeroed by the registry ctor and saved/loaded with the registry; the game speed itself is EngineConfig->timeWarpFactor (set by TI natives), which this native does NOT touch. Answers 0. Not verified by a full xref scan of the AP field (+0xc of the registry) - a reader elsewhere is possible.

name: INS_SetFocus
summary: Sets the base field of view used by all cockpits' sector cameras.
semantics: No cockpit handle. CockpitRegistry->baseFov = arg1 (raw binary angle, 65536 = 360 deg; default 16384 = 90 deg; stock: (degrees << 16) / 360). Each frame the cockpit update sets its sector/galaxy/dust camera focus to baseFov / zoom (clamped to a minimum); new cockpits copy it into their sectorFov at INS_CockpitAlloc. Saved with the registry. Answers 0.

name: INS_CockpitDoTracking
summary: Starts a target search on the cockpit: the object under the crosshair becomes the target after a delay.
semantics: All INS arguments are read as raw cell dwords (types are not checked); a cockpit handle is looked up with Cockpit::FindByHandle in the registry's hash map. Cockpit::SetTracking(cockpit, 1 searching, NULL): plays sound 1 if the state was not already 1, clears registry alert flag 0x80, sets 0x20000, trackedObject = NULL, state = 1, trackingTime = game time. Tracking state machine (Cockpit::SetTracking AP 0x00425a10, driven by the target overlay update): 0 cleared, 1 searching, 2 target assigned, 3 target locked, 4 enemy searching. While searching (1/4), once at least 1 s has passed since the search started, each update picks a candidate - state 1: the object under the crosshair (Cockpit::GetCursorAim(-1,-1,broad)); state 4: the nearest hostile (Cockpit::FindNearestHostile) - and goes to 2 (sound, registry alert flags 0x80/0x20000); after 1 more s in state 2 it goes to 3 (locked) and calls the script method NotifyTargetLock(target id, cockpit ship id) when the cockpit has a ship. When the tracked object disappears in states 2/3 it falls back to 1 and calls NotifyTargetLost(cockpit ship id) (class 0x96). Unknown cockpit: nothing. Answers 0.

name: INS_CockpitDoEnemyTracking
summary: Starts an enemy search on the cockpit: the nearest hostile becomes the target after a delay.
semantics: All INS arguments are read as raw cell dwords (types are not checked); a cockpit handle is looked up with Cockpit::FindByHandle in the registry's hash map. Cockpit::SetTracking(cockpit, 4 enemy searching, NULL): as INS_CockpitDoTracking but state 4 (sound 1 if not already 4). Tracking state machine (Cockpit::SetTracking AP 0x00425a10, driven by the target overlay update): 0 cleared, 1 searching, 2 target assigned, 3 target locked, 4 enemy searching. While searching (1/4), once at least 1 s has passed since the search started, each update picks a candidate - state 1: the object under the crosshair (Cockpit::GetCursorAim(-1,-1,broad)); state 4: the nearest hostile (Cockpit::FindNearestHostile) - and goes to 2 (sound, registry alert flags 0x80/0x20000); after 1 more s in state 2 it goes to 3 (locked) and calls the script method NotifyTargetLock(target id, cockpit ship id) when the cockpit has a ship. When the tracked object disappears in states 2/3 it falls back to 1 and calls NotifyTargetLost(cockpit ship id) (class 0x96). Unknown cockpit: nothing. Answers 0.

name: INS_CockpitIsTracking
summary: Returns 1 while the cockpit is in the 'searching' tracking state (started by INS_CockpitDoTracking).
semantics: All INS arguments are read as raw cell dwords (types are not checked); a cockpit handle is looked up with Cockpit::FindByHandle in the registry's hash map. Answers (trackingState == 1). It is 0 once a target was found (states 2/3), during an enemy search (4) and for an unknown cockpit; use INS_CockpitGetTracking for the target itself.

name: INS_CockpitGetCursorAim
args: cockpit:int | cockpit:int, x:int, y:int | cockpit:int, x:int, y:int, broad:bool
returns: int: object id under the cursor/crosshair, 0 if none
summary: Returns the object the cockpit's crosshair (or a given screen point) aims at.
semantics: All INS arguments are read as raw cell dwords (types are not checked); a cockpit handle is looked up with Cockpit::FindByHandle in the registry's hash map. argc <= 2: x = y = -1 (the crosshair, the middle of the cockpit camera's viewport), broad = false; argc >= 3: x = arg2, y = arg3 (screen pixels); argc >= 4: broad = CellIsTrue(arg4). Cockpit::GetCursorAim (AP 0x00425410): needs the cockpit ship and sector (else 0). First the target overlay's icon under the point (if it is an acceptable object); else a search of the sector's object lists for objects in front of the view along the aim ray (through the screen point via the sector camera), not destroyed/released/dummy/hull-less/scanner-hidden, not the own ship, specials only with a name: narrow = the ray passes within radius/2 of the object's centre; broad = objects within ~10 deg of the axis always count, others within 3/4 radius. Nearest within 5 km wins, or (when none within 5 km) one within 20x its radius. Quirk: the 32 class lists are scanned in order and the first list with a candidate wins even if a later class has a nearer object. Answers the object id or 0. With an explicit point (x >= 0 and y >= 0) and no icon hit, the sector camera is used to unproject the point WITHOUT a NULL check: a cockpit that has a ship and a sector but no INS_CockpitSetSectorCamera crashes the game.

name: INS_CockpitGetEnemyAim
returns: int: object id of the nearest hostile, 0 if none
summary: Returns the nearest hostile object within 5 km of the cockpit's view origin.
semantics: All INS arguments are read as raw cell dwords (types are not checked); a cockpit handle is looked up with Cockpit::FindByHandle in the registry's hash map. Cockpit::FindNearestHostile (AP 0x004258f0): needs the cockpit ship (else 0) and the cockpit sector (INS_CockpitSetSectorSpace). Over all 32 object lists of the sector: objects other than the ship that are hostile to it (relation check), not released/dummy/destroyed/hull-less and not scanner-hidden; distance (float) from the view origin (current view point of the ship, else its position) < 5000 m; the nearest wins. Answers its id or 0.
